24.en: Information is one of the most dangerous weapons the Inquisition wields, and the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.7ueULcEt4hF8R4dr]{Explicator} is a meticulous purveyor of this resource in all its forms. They are versed in various forbidden subjects, seeking out the depths of heretical and daemonic rituals, tomes, and dissertations via dusty research or actively pursuing new lines of inquiry in the field. Venturing blind into any encounter against the Imperium’s enemies means almost certain death.

28.en: It is indispensable for Inquisitorial agents to have the ear of an ally with extensive knowledge of the Imperial laws, doctrines, and loopholes that intersect with seeking out heretical practices and influences. Their duty demands they cut through bureaucratic roadblocks to find the quickest path for Inquisitors to assert their limitless authority. The Explicator is no stuffy librarian; they are as well-versed in the arts of swift retribution as any acolyte in an Inquisitor’s retinue.

32.en: Explicators are primarily drawn from Imperial factions that curate massive amounts of data. The most exceptional adepts of the Adminstratum are chief among their kin — rescued from the obscurity of datavaults and given greater purpose. Depending on where they specialise, Explicators can make excellent @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.z058E7qKD4CHpvoA]{Admonitors}, @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.N8aC89bUnEc78hRE]{Analyticus}, and @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.CB859tnMPuPPp7wz]{Xenolinguists}. However, their function may rely upon how well they can withstand the heresies they face. They are effectively students of the Ruinous Powers and the vile xenos, but only in order to facilitate their elimination, disgusted and fascinated by their research in equal measure.

36.en: Those chosen for this role must have a nimble and highly analytical mind. As much as the Inquisition requires of its storied warriors, you must meet the same criteria as a wielder of law and information. Like the @UUID[.j7wtNMhT96bMRSng]{Cruciator}, you will have access to texts far beyond the average scribe’s remit — corruptive materials that have no place in the hands of any righteous citizen. But this you must endure to serve Emperor, Inquisitor, and Ordo, to unravel the sordid mysteries and secretive plots that heretics and cultists so pride themselves on.
